content:
maria_nguyen: heads up — i'm prototyping an automatic fallback signal flow for rollouts. goal: reduce noisy manual interventions while keeping a clear audit trail. thoughts?

jonathan_cho: nice. can you sketch the high-level triggers you want to use? latency / 5xx / quality regressions? :thinking:

maria_nguyen: yep all three. rough idea:
- soft-degrade: if p95 latency > 900ms for 3m, move to a degraded instance (lower batch size)
- hard-degrade: if error-rate > 2% for 2m OR quality regression (eval set drift) then fallback to a compatible variant/model
- safety-cut: if combined resource OOM events or region outage -> global routing fallback

anya_patel: how do we detect "quality regression" automatically without a ton of false positives? eval sets are noisy.

maria_nguyen: good call. plan is hybrid: automated alert if model-level metric drop > X on canary prompt set AND user-facing trigger (increased re-roll ratio or human flags). automated action only if both signals present or if error-rate spikes.

ux_sam: from UX side we need to show these signals in the rollout panel and make the action reversible in one click. must surface rationale: e.g. "p95 latency 1.2s -> soft-degrade" so engs know why.

kevin_liu: audit-wise we should record: condition matched, config snapshot, triggered-by (system vs manual), and hashes of the model variants. make them queryable via Console + API.

maria_nguyen: yes. proposal: every automatic action writes an audit-entry: `{"time": ..., "trigger": "p95_latency", "value": "1200ms", "policy_id": "pf-23", "action": "soft-degrade", "actor": "autoscaler"}`

jonathan_cho: +1. also include topology info (region, pool id) and active routing decision so rollback can reproduce.

ops-bot: policy pf-23 created by maria_nguyen at 1962104350.

anya_patel: what about quotas? if fallback routes traffic to a more expensive pool, we need quota checks and an opt-in escalation path. otherwise we'll blow customer's spend.

maria_nguyen: absolutely. policy will check route capacity and projected cost delta. if cost delta > threshold -> open a pending escalation in Console requiring explicit approval. automated fallback only proceeds if cost delta < threshold OR team has override flag.

ux_sam: UI idea: show a compact timeline in rollout details with markers for each trigger and a hover card showing the 3 most recent metrics + the exact policy that fired. also allow filtering to only show automatic actions.

kevin_liu: for telemetry we should emit structured events to kafka: `fallback.triggered`, `fallback.rolled_back`, `fallback.decision.prefs` with tags: policy_id, model_hash, tenant_id, reason. make them high-cardinality safe (sample if necessary).

jonathan_cho: on internal API debate: do we expose a single "fallback.execute" endpoint that does check+apply+audit, or split check (dry-run) + apply? I prefer split so UI can preview.

maria_nguyen: split makes sense. endpoint plan: POST /policies/:id/preview -> returns actions + cost estimate + simulated audit entry. POST /policies/:id/execute -> performs checks, applies action, returns audit id.

anya_patel: add a dry-run mode to canary deploys too. engineers should be able to simulate the fallback on production traffic sample without committing.

ops-bot: note: remember to add guards for flapping (min time between auto-actions = 10m) and exponential backoff on retries.

maria_nguyen: adding that to the doc. also adding a TTL for auto-fallbacks so they don't persist forever (default 30m).

kevin_liu: we also need a retention policy for audit entries (default 90d) with export to bucket for legal + compliance.

ux_sam: final UX ask: if a user manually overrides an auto action, show a prominent "manual override" badge and who/why. we should disallow auto re-apply for at least X hours unless explicitly re-enabled.

jonathan_cho: ops playbook: add steps to verify model correctness after fallback and how to escalate to infra if it's capacity-related.

maria_nguyen: thanks — i'll open a short RFC with diagrams and sample console mocks. will include the JSON schema for audit events and the API endpoints.

anya_patel: lgtm. small nit: define exact thresholds for quality drift and re-roll ratio in RFC, maybe allow per-tenant overrides.

kevin_liu: +1. also log the pre-action KV cache hit rates — they often explain perf regressions.

maria_nguyen: noted. i'll include that metric and a sample query. thanks everyone.

jonathan_cho: ping me when RFC is up, happy to review the telemetry bits. :eyes:

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: review rfc draft with eng-platform on 1962105400.
